title: First survey
note: Photographed both street beds. Street Bed 1 still in heavy bloom and badly under-deadheaded. Street Bed 2 mostly finished and full of ripe poppy seed. Two plants unidentified, gladiolus showing possible thrips damage, one stalk with a long vertical split.

title: Questions answered
note: The woolly spikes are snapdragons, no lupines in either street bed. Split stem closed, nothing obvious on the ground. Gladiolus already overwinter in these beds and get lifted and spread each fall, so the corm question is settled: keep the existing routine and add a corm inspection while they are up. Still open: whether the whorled spike plant is veronica or agastache.

title: Inventory rebuilt around what is actually known
note: Seven of nineteen plants are not confirmed, including a large silver-grey mound in Street Bed 2 that has no identification at all, small blue flowers and a round-leaved plant in Street Bed 1, and a question over whether crocosmia is mixed in with the gladiolus. Some plantings were volunteers and are not remembered, so the plan is to photograph properly, check the camera roll from bloom time, stake the unknowns and revisit in spring.

title: Side bed added
note: Narrow raised bed along the house foundation: strawberries still flowering and fruiting, beans on string trellis, sunflowers against the wall, compost tumbler at the end. Sunflowers have clear powdery mildew, almost certainly from still air and a rain shadow next to the wall. Strawberries fruiting in late August means everbearing, so no mowing. Exposure for this bed not yet confirmed. Three of six areas mapped.

title: Site plan drawn from the sketch
note: Hand-drawn map turned into an interactive plan, north at top. Nine areas total, three surveyed. Orientation confirmed as south-up on the original sketch, which settles sun for every bed without asking: Back Bed 2 on the south wall is the hottest and driest spot, the Front Bed on the north wall is the shadiest ground on the property, and the Side Bed faces west, which explains the mildew. The two photographed beds are Street Bed 1 and Street Bed 2.

title: Bed Path surveyed
note: Fourth area. Rosemary, sage, a large stand of shasta daisy gone to seed, bearded iris, a possible euphorbia and a woody volunteer seedling. Mediterranean planting thriving, which is the evidence for full sun and sharp drainage. Key point recorded: this bed must not get the standard fall cut-back, and the iris division window closes in mid-September.

title: Correction: Back Bed 2 is not the sunny spot
note: The unlabelled box on the sketch is an easement, and beyond it stand two or three storey townhomes, close. That reverses the earlier call that Back Bed 2 was the best growing spot on the property. Boxed between the house to the north and tall buildings to the south, it gets a few hours of midday sun in high summer and effectively none from September through March. Reclassified as part sun, warm sheltered shade. The easement itself is plantable. Net effect: every genuinely sunny bed is out by the street, and everything against the house is shade or part shade.
